title: How was your grandparents' childhood different from yours?
examples: What was life like when my grandparents were young?
How does society change over time?

explain.say: If your grandmother wanted to talk to a cousin in another country in 1965, she might write a letter and wait weeks for a reply. You can video call in seconds! Look at the board: your grandparents' childhood on the left, yours on the right.

faq.q: How has childhood changed since the 1960s?
faq.a: Children today usually have more screens, faster communication, smaller families and longer schooling, while many grandparents remember more outdoor play, fewer toys and slower news. Love of play, friends and stories has stayed the same.
asks: How was life different for my grandparents?

faq.q: What was life like for children in the 1960s?
faq.a: In many places children played outside more, had fewer toys, shared one TV if they had one, wrote letters to faraway family, and often had more brothers and sisters.

faq.q: What is different about childhood today?
faq.a: Children today often have the internet, video calls, on-demand shows and online games, and in many countries they spend more years in school than their grandparents did.
Society changes because of new inventions like phones, new ideas about fairness and rights, new laws, and big events like wars or pandemics. Each generation grows up in a slightly different world.
asks: Why do things change over time?

faq.q: Is life better now than in the past?
faq.a: In many ways yes: people live longer, more children go to school and fewer babies die. But people debate some changes, like screen time or pollution, and older people remember good things that have faded.
asks: Was life better in the old days?

facts: In 1960, the average woman worldwide had about 5 children; by 2021 it was about 2.3 (UN World Population Prospects).
World life expectancy rose from about 50 years in 1960 to about 73 years in 2023 (UN).

quiz.say: In the 1960s, how did most people send a message to family in another country?
quiz.show: In the 1960s, a message abroad was usually…
quiz.why: Letters were the usual way, and they could take days or weeks.

wrong.1: Video calls became common only in the 2000s and 2010s.

quiz.say: Which of these has stayed the same for children across generations?
quiz.why: Children in every generation love play, friends and stories, even if the tools change.

wrong.0: Smartphones are new; grandparents did not have them as children.
wrong.2: On-demand shows are a recent change.
